doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

title: Blindfold test, first record memory and goodbyes
summary: Rowe plays an audio clip; Gordon recalls Tex Williams on a 78 as his first record, then they say goodbye.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: So Jerry I’m going to play, to wrap up, you might remember the blindfold tests that they used to run in DownBeat.
Yeah well I have one for you, it’s very brief. I don’t know if it would make your desert list, but see if you remember this. Are you ready?
If it’s an Evidence CD then I don’t remember.
It’s going to be a bad way to end this interview. Go ahead. I won’t ruin your surprise.

Oh my God, one of my favorite solos ever. That was my first record. I think that’s really why I got into jazz, honestly. We had a 78 player, that was Tex Williams, “Smoke Smoke Smoke that Cigarette.” And maybe I was three years old. I had a little child’s like baby- like chair that was a hand-me-down from my sister. And we had a 78 player and my parents would sit me down in front of the 78 player, thank you for playing that, and they would play “Smoke Smoke Smoke that Cigarette.” And it had that swing violin solo in the middle of it. And my parents, who were not particularly musical people, they were just like hard-working people and they did not sit and play records, although they owned some. They would sit me down and I would listen to that, and they would sing it and they would laugh, they all thought the lyrics to that song were the absolute greatest thing ever. And tell St. Peter at the Golden Gate that’s not even my background. But we loved it and everybody was singing it. So yeah, that might be it. That preceded “Kind of Blue” and “Man from Two Worlds” in my jazz education. Thank you for that.
Well it’s a long way from “Smoke that Cigarette” to Sun Ra so I’m appreciative of your career and for sharing everything you did today, Jerry.
Yeah thank you so much, both of you were great interviewers and it was a lot of fun for me. Thank you very much.
All right Christian, thanks a lot.
Thank you. So we are out.
